01 / The commission

Advance one.
Create another.

The achievement is a shared orchestration envelope with distinct project boundaries, rather than a single combined product.

The first track advanced UpFarm, an existing ecology of business simulators whose first working vertical models farm and aquaculture systems. Phase 2 added persistence and an operations journal while keeping records separate from simulation actions.

The second track became Cyber Red/Blue, a new educational game set inside the fictional Harbour Street Bakery network. It turns budgets, incomplete evidence and service availability into decisions.

The conversation records an initial block on Task B because an earlier game could not be found. A later agent report says a new build was authorised. This was a staged delivery; the retrieved record does not establish simultaneous execution or a recovered game.

02 / TRACK A · EXTEND THE LIVING SYSTEM

UpFarm.
A world with memory.

Ecology, aquaculture, production and the market already formed a working loop. Phase 2 gives that loop a durable record: autosave, portable JSON saves, an editable operator journal and a derived summary.

Play UpFarm ↗Download app ↓
01

Keep the next day

Changes save to the browser with visible save status. Corrupt and unavailable storage paths are covered by core tests.

02

Record the work

Add, edit, delete and filter operator entries. Simulation records are read-only. Operator records do not alter the simulated world.

03

Read the consequences

Summary totals, recent activity, inspection recency and operational alerts turn records into a useful review surface.

Boundary worth preserving.

The project’s design sequence is Observation → Inference → Authority → Action. Recording a pond observation grants no authority to control equipment. No actuator integration is part of this delivery.

The simulator still uses randomness. The Phase 2 core tests passing does not make the whole simulation deterministic.

03 / TRACK B · BUILD THE ADVERSARIAL WORLD

Cyber Red/Blue.
Keep the bakery open.

Red tries to steal the customer database. Blue must identify the threat, contain it and keep the shop trading. More defence is not always better: availability below 30% is a loss.

26 / 26 core testsWin paths, evidence, replay and isolation
10 roundsRed acts; Blue observes and responds
3 modesPlay Red · Play Blue · Hot-seat
8 nodes / 7 linksOne fictional business network
Play CyberRedBlue ↗Download app ↓
01

Limited resources, visible trade-offs

Red starts with 12 budget; Blue with 10. Actions have costs and conditions. Isolation can contain an intrusion while reducing availability.

02

Evidence is not ground truth

Unmonitored activity may remain unseen. Benign decoys complicate triage. Hot-seat offers an umpire view; solo modes also provide an explicit spoiler view.

03

Replay the reasoning

Deterministic rules make identical move sequences repeatable. The after-action report explains results, scores and missed evidence.

Fictional by construction.

The game operates on abstract browser state. The source isolation test rejects networking and code-execution APIs. Fresh offline runs observed no external requests.

One scenario, simple deterministic opponents, no save/load, and no claim of realistic attack modelling. MITRE ATT&CK labels are orientation aids.

A small evidence correction.

The earlier report said “14 Blue responses”. The current core exports 13 Blue action types, including Monitor and wait. Red has 10. Targets create additional selectable options; they are not extra action types.

Sources, provenance and image attribution

Evidence scope: The original local review examined project code, standalone exports, tests and recorded browser checks. This edition provides a sanitized verification summary. Private conversation records and machine-specific evidence are excluded.

Historical limits: The account of one originating brief comes from pasted agent reports. The full original task packet, separate new-game approval message and independent execution log were unavailable. Simultaneous execution is not established.

Images: Seven embedded PNG screenshots depict the included applications using verification data in fresh browser contexts, according to the original review. The brass twin-engine illustration and topology are original explanatory vector artwork; they are not application screenshots. No existing user saves are included.

Attribution: Application code and UI remain attributable to their respective projects. The original portfolio edition grants no additional distribution or licensing rights.

07 / What carries forward

The work behind the spectacle.

Ⅰ

Scope is part of the output.

Advancing an existing app and creating a new game require different starting assumptions. An explicit decision gate kept an unfound project from quietly becoming an invented recovery.

Ⅱ

Separate rules from rendering.

Both projects expose cores that can be exercised without a page. That makes validation, persistence edge cases and deterministic game outcomes inspectable before clicking through the interface.

Ⅲ

Delivery includes the doorway.

A claim of a working app becomes useful when the recipient has the executable file, a safe relative play link and a reproducible check. Packaging closes the gap between a progress report and something you can use.

Isolation, precisely stated.

This report blocks network connections, embedded frames, objects and form submission through its Content Security Policy. App links open separate documents with noopener noreferrer. The apps retain their original simulation and game scripts, with a shared appearance layer, and are not sandboxed by this report. Separate files and source folders are verified; OS-level isolation is not claimed.
